newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori suffers popularity dive - poll.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori suffers popularity dive - poll.

text.p: The popularity of Peru's President Alberto Fujimori has plummeted to 47 percent due to scandals in the security services and his administration's attacks on the Constitutional Court, a leading pollster said on Friday.
The Apoyo SA survey, conducted between May 9 and 11, also showed 44 percent of 503 adults in the capital disapprove of Fujimori's performance.
His popularity level was down 20 percent from the 67 percent registered a day after the successful April 22 raid at the besieged Japanese ambassador's home, which ended the Lima hostage crisis.

"The accusations against the intelligence service (SIN) and the attacks by the government against the Constitutional Court have had a negative effect on Fujimori, according to people interviewed," Apoyo analyst Jorge Aragon told Reuters.
Peru's highest military court last week sentenced four army intelligence officers to eight years in jail for the torture of a colleague suspected of leaking information to the media.

Fujimori has also been hit by disapproval of attempts to pressure the Constitutional Court and amend the judicial system in order to be allowed to run for re-election in 2000. The constitution is unclear on whether he can run again.
The poll also showed that Alberto Andrade, the increasingly popular mayor of Lima and possible 2000 presidential candidate, has a 70 percent approval rating, up from 65 percent in April.
The poll gave a margin of error of 4.5 percent.
